scenario: My weekend opened up earlier than I expected.
optionA: I pick something I have wanted to try and start right away.
optionB: I take a moment to see what I could do, then decide.

scenario: I notice an area at home that I want to organize.
optionA: I picture where things should go before I start.
optionB: I start with what is in front of me and tidy as I go.

scenario: I have some extra time in a neighborhood I have never visited.
optionA: I wander into places that catch my eye and explore as I go.
optionB: I look up what is nearby and decide where to go first.

scenario: I feel like starting a new hobby.
optionA: I look into what might suit me before I begin.
optionB: I choose something easy to try and give it a go first.

scenario: I am just starting a new assignment.
optionA: I begin with something I can do and figure things out as I go.
optionB: I look over what needs to be done before choosing my first task.

scenario: An idea worth trying comes up in a meeting.
optionA: I think through whether it makes sense and decide how to approach it.
optionB: I try it on a small scale and decide what to do next from there.

scenario: I need to work with a program I have never used before.
optionA: I learn by clicking around and trying things out.
optionB: I scan how it works before I start the task.

scenario: I am given a task with plenty of time before the deadline.
optionA: I first write down what I need and the order I will tackle it in.
optionB: I make a small early version so I can get a feel for the work.

scenario: A friend and I decide to try something new together.
optionA: I suggest one promising idea and try it first.
optionB: We talk a little more about what we each want to do before deciding.

scenario: Someone I know invites me to a new group or gathering.
optionA: I learn a bit about the group before deciding whether to go.
optionB: If it sounds fun, I go and see what it is like.

scenario: I unexpectedly get to spend a whole day with a friend.
optionA: We follow whatever feels appealing in the moment and fill the day as we go.
optionB: We first share what we want to do and put the day in some order.

scenario: Someone suggests that we start something new together.
optionA: I think through whether it is workable before we begin.
optionB: If it seems workable, I start with something small together.

scenario: It is the first meeting for an event we are preparing as a group.
optionA: I pick up something we can do now and get moving.
optionB: I look over everything that needs doing before we divide the work.

scenario: The team decides to try something new.
optionA: I want to agree on how we will do it before we start.
optionB: I want to try a little first and find the method as we go.

scenario: The general direction of a group project has been set.
optionA: We divide up the tasks that can be started right away.
optionB: We look at how the tasks depend on one another before dividing them up.

scenario: A good idea comes up in the group, but it is still vague.
optionA: I clarify what we will do and how before we start.
optionB: I start with what we can do now and fill in the rest as we go.

scenario: The place I planned to use suddenly becomes unavailable.
optionA: I move to another promising place and think about the next step from there.
optionB: I check a few possible places and then choose one.

scenario: I realize that something I am working on is different from what I expected.
optionA: I look at what changed and what it affects before I act.
optionB: I start with what I can do now and adjust as I go.

scenario: My schedule for the day suddenly changes a lot.
optionA: I start using the newly opened time and adjust the rest around it.
optionB: I look over the whole day again before I move forward.

scenario: An unfamiliar problem comes up unexpectedly.
optionA: I look at the problem a little more before taking action.
optionB: I try what I can do now and find a way forward as I go.

scenario: Several options all look promising.
optionA: I choose the one that feels most appealing now and move on.
optionB: I compare a few more and choose once I feel settled.

scenario: I want to buy something, but there are too many similar choices.
optionA: I put a few candidates side by side and compare them before choosing.
optionB: When one catches my eye and fits what I wanted, I choose it.

scenario: I need to choose a direction even though some things are still unknown.
optionA: I decide with what I know now and adjust as I move forward.
optionB: I find out what else I can before making the decision.

scenario: I have to choose between two plans.
optionA: I think about what each choice could affect later before deciding.
optionB: When one feels more important, I choose it and move on.

scenario: I am deciding how to divide household chores with someone I live with.
optionA: We talk about what is comfortable for each of us and coordinate who does what.
optionB: I decide what is mine to handle and do it in my own way.

scenario: I am traveling with someone, and we want to visit different places.
optionA: We each pick the places we really want to see and spend the rest of the time separately.
optionB: We connect the places we each want to see into a route we can enjoy together.

scenario: A friend and I are cooking together.
optionA: We keep track of where we are and divide the tasks as we go.
optionB: I take one dish and make it from start to finish on my own.

scenario: I need to choose a major purchase with someone close to me.
optionA: We agree on what matters, then each look for options separately.
optionB: We work out what matters together and narrow the options as a pair.

scenario: We need to decide who will handle what on a shared project.
optionA: We keep talking about what each person is doing and coordinate as we go.
optionB: I take responsibility for my part and handle it in my own way.

scenario: A coworker and I have somewhat different work habits.
optionA: We agree on what needs to be delivered and each decide how to get there.
optionB: We find a way of working that is comfortable for both of us and adjust to each other.

scenario: Several ideas come up at once in a meeting.
optionA: I look for the overlap and bring related ideas together.
optionB: I give each idea to someone to develop separately, then compare them later.

scenario: Someone on a shared project suddenly needs to change their schedule.
optionA: We decide only what needs to be handed off, and each person rearranges their own schedule.
optionB: We look at everything together and revise roles and dates as a group.

scenario: I am planning a get-together with friends who have very different tastes.
optionA: I plan it so different preferences are represented across the group.
optionB: I leave room for people to spend some time doing what they personally prefer.

scenario: I am preparing something together with someone close to me.
optionA: I trust them with their part and step in only when needed.
optionB: We check in often on how things are going and keep adjusting together.

scenario: During a group conversation, two people strongly disagree.
optionA: I look for a point both can accept and help the conversation continue.
optionB: I let each person fully express their view and leave the choice to them.

scenario: A friend and I decide to work toward the same goal.
optionA: We each do it our own way and share how it went on an agreed date.
optionB: We check our progress and keep our pace roughly aligned.

scenario: A group needs to divide several roles.
optionA: I match roles by connecting what people are good at with what they want to do.
optionB: I make each role's goal clear and leave the rest to the person responsible.

scenario: There are several opinions about something we are creating together.
optionA: The people who suggested each idea build their own version, then we compare them.
optionB: We combine the different ideas into one approach the whole group can use.

scenario: People on the team work at different speeds.
optionA: We shift roles around so the team can stay more in sync.
optionB: I let each person work at their own pace within their role.

scenario: We need to decide a new way to run a group.
optionA: We set only what is essential and leave the rest to the people responsible.
optionB: We gather everyone's input and create a shared way of working.

scenario: One person can no longer make a day we had planned together.
optionA: We ask about everyone's availability again and find another day that works for all.
optionB: We reschedule only the parts that truly need everyone and separate the rest.

scenario: Someone on the team suddenly cannot complete their assigned work.
optionA: We split the work, assign new owners, and let each person handle their part.
optionB: We look again at what each person can do and redistribute the work together.

scenario: Something we planned to do together suddenly changes.
optionA: We get together and talk through who will do what again.
optionB: I check what changed and reorganize my own part first.

scenario: An unexpected problem requires several people to respond together.
optionA: We quickly divide roles and let each person use their own judgment.
optionB: We keep track of what everyone is doing and coordinate our actions.

scenario: People want different things in a decision we need to make together.
optionA: I look for an option that as many people as possible can feel comfortable with.
optionB: I shape the decision so people still have room to choose for themselves.

scenario: I get to choose who I will work with.
optionA: I choose someone who can own their part and handle it in their own way.
optionB: I choose someone who seems likely to work in sync with me.

scenario: Several people are editing one piece of writing together.
optionA: We coordinate which parts to edit so our work does not overlap.
optionB: We assign sections and each person edits their own section independently.

scenario: A group needs to decide what to do next.
optionA: We keep several options open and let the person responsible choose.
optionB: We gather everyone's views and choose the option with the most common ground.

scenario: I am thinking about redesigning one part of a room.
optionA: I imagine several looks that feel very different from how it is now.
optionB: I decide what should go where based on the space and how it will be used.

scenario: I am making a meal with ingredients I use often.
optionA: I choose an easy dish that fits the ingredients I have.
optionB: I imagine a new dish by combining familiar ingredients in an unusual way.

scenario: I want to organize my photos or personal records.
optionA: I think of an interesting way to group them that feels different from the usual.
optionB: I sort them by clear features such as date or subject.

scenario: I am choosing a gift for someone.
optionA: I picture when and how that person would use it, then choose.
optionB: I imagine several things that person would never expect.

scenario: I get a chance to improve a routine task.
optionA: I imagine several ways of doing it differently from now.
optionB: I identify something concrete that I can improve right away.

scenario: I need to set the overall direction for a new project.
optionA: I first define clearly who it is for and what we are making.
optionB: I spread out several possible directions and explore them broadly.

scenario: I can choose how to present something.
optionA: I come up with a way to show it that people may not have seen before.
optionB: I organize the main points in order and add examples.

scenario: I am asked to suggest several ways to solve a problem.
optionA: I list practical things we could try right away, one by one.
optionB: I also imagine approaches that are completely different from what we do now.

scenario: I am helping prepare something for a friend's special day.
optionA: I think of something unusual that could become a memorable experience.
optionB: I plan around what the person likes and the time we have.

scenario: I am looking for something fun to do with someone I know.
optionA: I look for options that fit the available time and place.
optionB: I freely imagine things we have never tried before.

scenario: Someone asks me to add ideas to their plan.
optionA: I suggest a new direction that could open up their thinking.
optionB: I suggest a practical way to help them carry it out.

scenario: I am preparing a small event with friends.
optionA: I plan the sequence so people can enjoy themselves comfortably.
optionB: I imagine a fresh concept that could change the whole atmosphere.

scenario: The team needs to decide what to work on next.
optionA: I connect different ideas to create something unexpected.
optionB: I narrow the options based on the goal and the number of people involved.

scenario: We can freely choose the form of something we are making together.
optionA: I choose a form that makes its intended use immediately clear.
optionB: I explore several formats we have not used before.

scenario: A group is designing a new recurring program.
optionA: I imagine a new program that combines different fields or themes.
optionB: I build the program around the time available and the sequence of activities.

scenario: The team suggests finding new uses for things we already have.
optionA: I look for practical uses that are possible with what we already have.
optionB: I imagine uses far beyond what those things were originally meant for.

scenario: The method I planned to use is no longer available.
optionA: I open up completely different possibilities and rethink the approach.
optionB: I identify a practical way forward with what is still available.

scenario: I suddenly have to work with unexpected materials or tools.
optionA: I look at each item's intended use and find a practical way to use it.
optionB: I try combining things in new ways and experiment.

scenario: I need to set something up in a place I have never seen before.
optionA: I draw new possibilities from what feels unique about the space.
optionB: I look at how people will move through the space and where the facilities are, then place things accordingly.

scenario: A plan I made is not working as well as expected.
optionA: I look at what has happened so far and identify what can be improved.
optionB: I reframe the problem and look for a new direction.

scenario: I need to choose one idea from several options.
optionA: I am drawn to the one that sparks ideas for what else could be added.
optionB: I am drawn to the one where I can clearly picture who will use it, when, and how.

scenario: I need to choose a topic for something new I will create.
optionA: I look for a topic with a clear picture of who would use it, when, and how.
optionB: I look for a topic that could connect with something unfamiliar.

scenario: I need to create something freely without a set topic.
optionA: I choose something that lets me combine things that are not usually put together.
optionB: I choose something I can complete with what I already have.

scenario: Two ways of solving a problem both look good.
optionA: I am drawn to the option whose outcome I can picture clearly right now.
optionB: I am drawn to the option that leaves more room to grow later.

scenario: I want to review how I spent money over the past month.
optionA: I break the spending into categories and see how much went to each.
optionB: I look at the month as a whole and see where the spending was concentrated.

scenario: Sometimes I want to change one of my daily habits.
optionA: I look at my whole daily pattern of eating, sleeping, and working.
optionB: I look back one by one at what I did and how I felt afterward.

scenario: I am choosing a new electronic device.
optionA: I compare features and prices side by side, category by category.
optionB: I consider how I will use it and how it will fit with my other devices.

scenario: Lately, it feels like I never have enough time.
optionA: I look at work, rest, and relationships as one overall pattern.
optionB: I break down where my time has gone by activity.

scenario: The result of my work turns out differently from what I expected.
optionA: I break the process into stages and look for where things went off track.
optionB: I look at how the whole process unfolded from beginning to end.

scenario: I need to reach a conclusion from several pieces of information.
optionA: I first look for the larger picture that the sources point to together.
optionB: I compare the evidence and differences in each source side by side.

scenario: I need to explain something complicated to someone.
optionA: I break it into smaller parts and explain them in order.
optionB: I focus on how the different parts connect to one another.

scenario: I need to evaluate a new proposal.
optionA: I look at how the proposal would fit with the work already underway.
optionB: I examine its assumptions and supporting reasons one by one.

scenario: A friend asks what I think about a complicated situation.
optionA: I separate out what happened and in what order.
optionB: I step back and look at how the people involved affect one another.

scenario: Several people tell somewhat different versions of the same situation.
optionA: I consider each person's position together with the atmosphere at the time.
optionB: I separate what matches across the accounts from what differs.

scenario: I am helping someone think through a choice they need to make.
optionA: I put the options side by side and compare how they differ.
optionB: I consider how the choice could connect with the life they want going forward.

scenario: I think about why a misunderstanding happened in a conversation.
optionA: I consider what had happened before and the atmosphere that day.
optionB: I pinpoint the point where we may have understood the same words differently.

scenario: A team activity did not go as well as expected.
optionA: I separate the process and look for where each person got stuck.
optionB: I step back and look at how the team worked together as a whole.

scenario: We look back after finishing something together.
optionA: I consider the overall change the work created.
optionB: I compare how far we got on each goal.

scenario: I need to compare proposals from several teams.
optionA: I use the same criteria to compare differences item by item.
optionB: I look at the larger changes each proposal could create over time.

scenario: Someone suggests that the way our group operates needs improvement.
optionA: I look at how the group runs together with people's overall experience of it.
optionB: I identify where problems happen and how often they occur.

scenario: A problem suddenly appears, and I do not know why.
optionA: I separate the visible clues one by one and narrow down the cause.
optionB: I look at what happened before and after the problem and connect the sequence.

scenario: Something unexpected keeps happening again and again.
optionA: I scan for broader changes around me that may have happened recently.
optionB: I compare when it happens and when it does not to find a pattern.

scenario: I try my usual way of doing things in a new place, but it does not work well.
optionA: I compare the details to find exactly where things begin to differ.
optionB: I look at how my usual approach fits with the way this place operates.

scenario: The things I have heard do not line up with one another.
optionA: I consider the circumstances before and after each statement was made.
optionB: I check each statement one by one to see where it came from.

scenario: I have gathered a lot of information before an important decision.
optionA: I set clear criteria and compare the options one by one.
optionB: I consider how the decision could shape my life going forward.

scenario: Two plans look similarly good.
optionA: I consider how each plan would affect other commitments and people.
optionB: I break the plans down and examine exactly how they differ.

scenario: I am deciding which of several explanations makes the most sense.
optionA: I check whether each claim follows logically from its supporting evidence.
optionB: I look at how well each explanation fits the situation as a whole.

scenario: I need to choose which problem to solve first.
optionA: I look at how the problems are connected and choose the one at the center.
optionB: I compare the size and cause of each problem and choose what to address first.

scenario: Someone close to me is quieter than usual.
optionA: I gently start a conversation so they can speak when they feel comfortable.
optionB: I mention what seems different and ask whether they are okay.

scenario: Someone close to me opens up about something they are struggling with.
optionA: I listen through to the end, then share what I understood and what I think.
optionB: I ask more about how they feel and follow where the conversation goes.

scenario: Someone looks like they may need my help.
optionA: I take time to understand what they need without making them feel pressured.
optionB: I say what I can help with and ask whether they want it.

scenario: Someone I am with seems to be in a very good mood.
optionA: I point out what seems good and congratulate them clearly.
optionB: I share their excitement and ask what made them happy.

scenario: A coworker seems to be taking a mistake very hard.
optionA: I listen to how it felt for them and give them room to say what they need to say.
optionB: I clarify what needs to happen now and what I can help with.

scenario: Someone cautiously shares an opinion in a meeting.
optionA: I reflect what I understood and state my own view clearly too.
optionB: I respond in a way that helps them keep talking and listen.

scenario: Someone I work with has seemed worn out lately.
optionA: I naturally check in and ask how things have been.
optionB: I mention what I have noticed and ask whether they need anything.

scenario: I need to give someone feedback.
optionA: I point out what I observed and what I think could be improved.
optionB: I think about how it may come across and choose my wording and order carefully.

scenario: A friend talks to me about a major decision they are facing.
optionA: I listen for what matters to them and help them sort through it.
optionB: I clearly tell them what seems most important from my point of view.

scenario: I realize that someone close to me and I saw the same situation differently.
optionA: I clearly share what I think and what I hope for going forward.
optionB: I first listen to how the other person felt at the time.

scenario: Someone I know shares good news with me.
optionA: I focus on how happy they are and celebrate the feeling with them.
optionB: I point out what is good about the news and clearly congratulate them.

scenario: A friend brings up the same concern several times.
optionA: I listen and honestly share what I have come to think about it.
optionB: I keep the conversation going while noticing how their feelings change each time.

scenario: Someone new to the group looks uncomfortable.
optionA: I read the atmosphere and start a conversation that helps them join in.
optionB: I clearly explain what is happening and what they can do.

scenario: Someone on the team is having trouble speaking up.
optionA: I ask them directly what they think and listen to their answer.
optionB: I leave space for them to speak and wait while watching their response.

scenario: We are talking together about something we just completed.
optionA: I listen to how each person experienced it and build the conversation from there.
optionB: I point out what went well and what could be changed.

scenario: Someone I worked with feels very disappointed about how things ended.
optionA: I clearly explain where we got to and what happens next.
optionB: I listen to what feels disappointing to them and pay attention to their feelings.

scenario: The other person's expression suddenly changes during a conversation.
optionA: I slow down and consider what may have made them uncomfortable.
optionB: I immediately ask whether something in what we just discussed bothered them.

scenario: A conflict suddenly comes up between us.
optionA: I clarify what the problem is and what each of us wants.
optionB: I keep the conversation going while paying attention to how each person feels.

scenario: I hear that someone I know has suddenly gone through something difficult.
optionA: I stay available and listen in the way that seems to fit what they need.
optionB: I contact them and clearly say what I can do to help.

scenario: Someone I was working with suddenly says they are stepping away.
optionA: I confirm what had been agreed and take care of the remaining work.
optionB: I first listen to what circumstances and feelings led to the decision.

scenario: A friend seems to want both comfort and my opinion.
optionA: I pay attention to what they seem to need and let the conversation unfold from there.
optionB: I honestly tell them what I think.

scenario: I am deciding when to bring up an important topic.
optionA: Once I know clearly what I want to say, I set a time and bring it up.
optionB: I look for a time when the other person seems comfortable and bring it up then.

scenario: I am unsure whether to offer my help.
optionA: I watch a little longer and ask naturally when it feels right.
optionB: I say what I can do and let the other person decide whether they want it.

scenario: We want different things and need to work out an agreement.
optionA: I first state clearly what I can and cannot do.
optionB: I first ask what matters most to the other person.

scenario: I have a few things I need to do every week.
optionA: I set specific days and times and keep the routine the same.
optionB: I look at that week's circumstances and fit them in where I can.

scenario: I need to keep my home organized on a regular basis.
optionA: I start with whatever feels most urgent that day.
optionB: I follow a set order and take care of each area when its turn comes.

scenario: I want to keep up a regular exercise or study routine.
optionA: I stick to the frequency and times I decided in advance.
optionB: I adjust the routine based on how I feel and what my schedule looks like.

scenario: I have several things to remember when I leave home.
optionA: I first pack what I need for where I am going that day.
optionB: I go through the same usual order and check each item.

scenario: I am responsible for a task with several stages.
optionA: I set the dates and sequence in advance and follow them.
optionB: I keep the goal in mind and change the order as needed along the way.

scenario: There is a task I do over and over.
optionA: I adjust how I do it to fit the circumstances that day.
optionB: I follow the same established method each time.

scenario: I am working on a long project with a distant deadline.
optionA: I set interim goals and review dates in advance.
optionB: I watch how things are going and adjust when to put in more effort.

scenario: I need to decide how to organize materials that build up through my work.
optionA: I adjust the way I sort them over time so they stay easy to find.
optionB: I create a common rule and organize them the same way each time.

scenario: I have a regular get-together with friends.
optionA: I try to keep the agreed date and format as consistently as possible.
optionB: I change the date and format to fit people's circumstances.

scenario: Someone close to me and I have an agreement we want to keep.
optionA: If our circumstances change, we revise the agreement together.
optionB: I keep the agreement in mind and try to follow it consistently.

scenario: Several people need to split a shared cost.
optionA: I divide it the same way we originally agreed each time.
optionB: I adjust how we split it when people's circumstances differ.

scenario: We need rules for a shared item or space.
optionA: I set only the main guidelines and let people handle the rest as they see fit.
optionB: I set clear rules for how it is used and have everyone follow the same rules.

scenario: The team regularly shares how far the work has progressed.
optionA: We share updates on a set schedule and in a consistent format.
optionB: We change the timing and format depending on how the work is going.

scenario: We are planning the sequence for a group event.
optionA: We leave room to change roles and the order on the day if needed.
optionB: We decide roles and the sequence in advance and follow the plan.

scenario: The team is creating new standards for how work should be done.
optionA: We set standards that can be applied the same way no matter who is doing the work.
optionB: We set the main guidelines and let each person adapt them to the situation.

scenario: Several people need to manage a shared deadline.
optionA: We adjust the dates as the work progresses.
optionB: We set the dates in advance and keep them as planned.

scenario: An unexpected issue comes up in a schedule I already planned.
optionA: I keep the dates that must stay fixed and move only what can be changed.
optionB: I rebuild the dates and sequence around the new situation.

scenario: My usual way of doing something does not fit well today.
optionA: I rearrange the order to fit today as well as possible.
optionB: I keep my usual approach and change only what is necessary.

scenario: An unexpected request comes in.
optionA: I keep my original priority order and fit the request into an open spot.
optionB: I reassess what is most urgent now and reorder everything.

scenario: Something changes suddenly while we are already working together.
optionA: I change the method and sequence right away to fit the situation.
optionB: I keep what we already agreed and look for another way to adapt.

scenario: I am choosing between two ways of working.
optionA: I choose the one that makes it easier to keep dates and standards consistent.
optionB: I choose the one that is easier to adjust when circumstances change.

scenario: I am deciding how to make a new habit last.
optionA: I choose an approach that lets me adjust from day to day.
optionB: I choose an approach with set times and frequency.

scenario: I need to set one standard that several people will use.
optionA: I first look for a standard that can be applied the same way to everyone.
optionB: I first look for a standard that can be adjusted to fit different circumstances.

scenario: I am choosing a tool to manage my schedule.
optionA: I choose one that makes it easy to move and rearrange plans.
optionB: I choose one that lets me see planned and completed tasks at a glance.
